item.text: At dawn, the forest rests beneath a thin veil of mist. Tall pines stand quietly along the slope, their dark trunks softened by moss and pale lichen. Between them, young birches lift silver branches toward the first light. The air is cool and clean, carrying the faint scents of damp earth, fallen needles, and wild mint. A narrow stream threads through the trees, barely louder than a whisper as it passes over smooth stones. Ferns bow along its banks, jeweled with droplets that catch the sunrise and briefly shine. Somewhere overhead, a bird gives one clear note, then settles into silence. No road or roof interrupts the view; the woods seem to continue beyond sight, growing dimmer and bluer with distance. In a small clearing, grass bends under the weight of dew. A single fox crosses its edge, paws soundless, red coat bright against the muted greens and browns. It pauses to listen, ears turned toward the stream, then slips beneath the bracken. Light spreads slowly through the canopy, touching one patch of bark, one cluster of leaves, and one mossy stone at a time. The forest remains calm, not empty but gently alive, keeping its own unhurried rhythm while morning gathers around it.
